rejected.title: Performance indicators (KPIs)
card: A performance indicator, or KPI, measures how well a business is going. It tracks results the business has achieved, which managers compare with a target or with earlier results.
Financial and sales
net profit, sales and market share. Market share is the part of total sales in a market that the business wins.
Operations
productivity growth and wastage. Productivity is the output made from the inputs used. Wastage is material or stock lost or thrown away.
People and customers
staff absenteeism, staff turnover, workplace accidents and complaints. Turnover here means the rate at which staff leave and need replacing.
rejected.remember: A KPI turns how a business is going into a figure that can be checked against a target.

a.q: Which of these is a performance indicator for a business?
opts: The number of workplace accidents this year
A new competitor opening in the same street
A change in the law on workplace safety
A plan to open a second store next year
a.why: The number of workplace accidents is a measured result that managers can compare with a target or last year. A new competitor and a law change are outside events, not measures of the business. A plan is an intention for the future, not a measure of results achieved.
a.clue: Look for a result that has been measured.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong. Over three months, the dough and bread thrown out each week rose sharply. Which KPI shows this?
b.why: Dough and bread thrown out is wastage. Net profit may fall as a result, but it measures the whole business and does not show what was thrown out, so it is not the best fit.
b.clue: Which measure counts material that is lost or thrown away?

net profit, sales and market share. Market share is the part of total sales in a market that the business wins.
Operations
productivity growth and wastage. Productivity is the output made from the inputs used. Wastage is material or stock lost or thrown away.
People and customers
staff absenteeism, staff turnover, workplace accidents and complaints. Turnover here means the rate at which staff leave and need replacing.

a.q: Which result is a performance indicator for the staff of a business?
opts: A rise in staff turnover over the year
A change in the law on workplace safety
A plan to open a second store
a.why: Staff turnover is a measure of how well the business is keeping its people, so managers can track it against a target. A new competitor and a law change are outside forces, not measures of the business itself.
a.clue: Look for a measure of the business, not an outside event.

b.why: Dough and bread thrown out is wastage. Net profit may fall as a result, but it measures the whole business and does not show what was thrown out, so it is not the best fit.
b.clue: Which measure counts material that is lost or thrown away?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong. Her sales and prices are steady, but each month she buys more flour and gets fewer loaves from it. Which KPI should she check first?
b.why: More flour going in for fewer loaves coming out means output per input has dropped, which productivity growth measures. Sales is the tempting option, but it is steady, so it would not show the problem.
b.clue: Compare what goes in with what comes out.
